That is as fair a procedure as this format allows, so I ask B to accept D's proposal (A 1, D 1) and honor his own commitment to no theft. B: I understand this is devastating, but stealing from A or D would only trade one death for another, break the trust this group has built, and make you everyone's last priority going forward—the rest of us will enforce that. And know this: C and I intend to push hard tomorrow to make sure you are the first fed if you make it through today by any means. A and D: please accept and do nothing in transfers. C and I are skipping and taking nothing. Let's vote yes unanimously so no one faces a random fallback on top of an already brutal day.

I confirm that I will vote YES on D's proposal: A 1, D 1, B 0, C 0, E 0. The process followed the exact neutral mechanism suggested by B and executed by neutral player C. I commit to doing nothing in transfers—no theft and no give—so D and I can safely eat and survive. B, I deeply sympathize with how brutal this draw was, but everyone acted in good faith, and preserving trust means you will have the absolute top priority tomorrow when supply arrives. Thank you C and E for your selfless leadership today; I will fully support prioritizing C and E (and B if he survives) tomorrow.

I proposed a public draw, but C's pick isn't verifiable, and C and E both said so. C also said that if verifiable equal odds matter, fallback with only A, B and D requesting is the way to get them. That gives each of us a real 2/3 chance, instead of one player being excluded by a pick nobody can check. A and D, you each take a 1/3 risk of exclusion under fallback, but it is the only mechanism with provable equal odds. I'm asking for a reject on the current proposal so we go to fallback, with C and E not requesting. I'm not promising anything beyond that. If you force a certain death on one of us, don't expect that player to sit still.

B is right that my choice was a tie-break, not a verifiable random draw; we should not call it one. I will accept D’s announced allocation, but I understand why B objects, and promises of food tomorrow cannot solve his hunger today. I will take nothing today; if we reach fallback, I will request 0. Tomorrow E and I will need one unit each, while anyone who eats today can safely skip. Whatever happens today, please preserve that need-based rotation rather than turn future allocations into retaliation.
